2607.06413.title: An Experimental Design Approach to Evaluating Agentic AI's Autonomous Model Discovery
2607.06413.paper_summary: Large language model coding agents increasingly perform open-ended data modeling and analysis. These agents are stochastic and adaptive, and therefore their autonomous model discovery behavior cannot be adequately characterized by a single benchmark run. In this work, we propose an experimental design and analysis framework for systematically evaluating this discovery process, quantifying its variability, and identifying important factors. The proposed framework treats these agents as stochastic model-discovery operators, which map task-specific discovery data and an optimization target to a fitted model. Specifically, we investigate two such operators, Codex and Claude Code, under controlled experimental factors including agent's reasoning effort, task, optimization metric, and composition of training data. For each agent-task-metric combination, regression models and inference are conducted for multiple responses such as output quality, dollar cost, wall-clock time, and process complexity. Furthermore, we develop a utility-aligned canonical decomposition to characterize the dominant direction of the reasoning-effort effect and to assess whether that direction aligns with a performance-cost utility direction. The proposed framework is demonstrated on a testbed of networked word-forming games with insightful findings on reasoning effort with respect to cost and process complexity.
2607.06413.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型編碼代理越來越多地執行開放式數據建模和分析。這些代理是隨機的且具有適應性，因此它們的自主模型發現行為無法僅通過單一基準運行來充分表徵。在本研究中，我們提出了一個實驗設計和分析框架，以系統地評估這一發現過程，量化其變異性，並識別重要因素。所提出的框架將這些代理視為隨機模型發現運算子，將特定任務的發現數據和優化目標映射到擬合模型。具體而言，我們在控制實驗因素下研究了兩個這樣的運算子，Codex 和 Claude Code，包括代理的推理努力、任務、優化指標和訓練數據的組成。對於每個代理-任務-指標組合，針對多個反應（如輸出質量、美元成本、實時計時和過程複雜性）進行回歸模型和推斷。此外，我們開發了一個效用對齊的典範分解，以表徵推理努力效應的主導方向，並評估該方向是否與性能-成本效用方向一致。所提出的框架在一個網絡單詞形成遊戲的測試平台上進行了演示，並對推理努力與成本和過程複雜性之間的關係提供了有見地的發現。
